title: handoff-routing-auth-bakeoff-recap-2027-06-02
notes:
Summary: Mini bakeoff + handoff focusing on routing decisions, auth token rotation impact, and quota enforcement gaps. This was a cross-squad 90-minute working session (no slides, whiteboard-heavy) to validate assumptions from last sprint and create a compact runbook for on-call engineers.

Attendees: Aisha (lead), Miguel (routing), Rina (auth), Evan (quota infra), Priya (SRE), Ben (platform observability), plus two rotating attendees from solutions-eng (Sam, Leah) for the customer-impact perspective.

Why we met
- Persistent incidents where the control plane routing fallback kicked in during multi-region mirror tests; unclear whether the cause was routing policy mis-evaluation, auth failures, or quota enforcement stalls.
- Need a short, practical handoff doc for next 2-week on-call rotation that covers triage steps and quick mitigations.
- Validate quick experiments Miguel ran for weighted fallthrough and Evan's quota backoff heuristics.

Key observations from the session
1) Routing fallthrough root causes
- Two main failure modes reproduced in lab: (a) short-lived auth token TTL expiry causing RPC rejects, (b) transient per-customer quota bookkeeping lag that made capacity appear exhausted.
- Weighted routing algorithm correctly prefers local-region pools but the graceful degrade path currently assumes any non-200 from the pool equals permanent fail — this leads to rapid global fallback instead of retrying compatible pools.
- Miguel's new judgment window (200ms) reduces unnecessary global fallbacks in lab when backend tails are <150ms.

2) Auth token rotation
- Rina showed logs where token rotation created a 1–2 second burst of 401s across multi-route callers because some clients cached older tokens and retried aggressively.
- The control plane has no staggered rotation; rotating all worker nodes at once amplifies the spike.
- Immediate mitigation: adopt staggered rotation windows and add a short grace window where old token remains accepted for up to 5s post-rotation.

3) Quota enforcement and bookkeeping
- Evan demonstrated a race where quota counters are incremented pre-commit and decremented on failure, but occasional commit ack drop leaves counters inflated for ~30s until reconciliation job runs.
- That inflation triggers per-customer soft-quota thresholds and causes upstream throttle signals that cascade into routing fallbacks.
- Proposed: fast reconciliation microtask that looks at unacknowledged ops within the last 60s and fixes counters; also expose a realtime counter-visibility endpoint for SRE to inspect during incidents.

Decisions and small experiments to run this sprint
- Routing: adopt Miguel's judgment window 200ms as default for canary 1.1 on dedicated capacity; observe global fallback rate metric (metric name: router.fallback.rate) for 72h. (Owner: Miguel, ticket PLAT-4823)
- Auth: implement staggered rotation and 5s grace acceptance on control plane tokens; add instrumentation for post-rotation 401 spike. Rollout to canary region only. (Owner: Rina, ticket AUTH-391)
- Quotas: Evan to implement a fast-reconcile job and a /debug/quota/counters endpoint (read-only) for SRE use. Tweak soft-quota amber thresholds to be more tolerant during reconciliation window. (Owner: Evan)

Action items (concrete)
- Miguel: push judgment-window change behind feature flag; create a canary to route 10% of traffic for 72h. Post canary, gather percentiles for fallback rate and p99 latency. Due: 2027-06-07.
- Rina: PR for staggered rotation + grace window; add alert rule that fires if post-rotation 401 rate > 0.5% above baseline for >60s. Due: 2027-06-06.
- Evan: fast reconciliation task PoC and read-only counters endpoint; add dashboard tile in Console showing in-flight vs committed token counts. Due: 2027-06-09.
- Priya: update on-call runbook with short triage flow (isolate auth / quota / routing) and escalation path to routing-owner, auth-owner, and quota-owner. Due: 2027-06-04.
- Ben: add temporary tracing tag to identify cross-service request hops when fallback increases (router->auth->quota). Due: 2027-06-05.

Triage playbook (short form) — for oncall
1) Check router.fallback.rate and p50/p95 latency at ingestion. If fallback spikes but backend latency stable, suspect auth or quota failures.
2) Inspect auth.401.rate and recent token rotation events — look for cluster-wide rotation at same timestamp.
3) Check quota counter diffs via /debug/quota/counters; if counters show large in-flight > committed discrepancy, trigger fast-reconcile and mute soft-quota alarms.
4) If none of the above, temporarily reduce judgment-window and enable local-only routing to maintain lowest-latency traffic while debugging.

Open questions
- Is 5s grace for token acceptance acceptable for compliance/regulatory customers? Rina to check with security/compliance; if not acceptable, we need an alternate tactic (e.g., token shadowing) before wide rollout.
- How much extra load does fast-reconcile create under peak? Evan to simulate with replay and include cost estimate.
- Should we surface per-customer quota anomaly alerts to product (customer success) for high-value customers? Priya to propose thresholds.

Notes on communication
- Customer-facing incidents: Sam/Leah to draft a short template for customer success that explains transient fallbacks and the mitigation steps; keep it non-technical.
- Internal postmortem plan: if fallback spike affects >5% of requests for >1h, we will trigger a lightweight PM-led incident review and include screenshots of fallback metric + auth 401 spikes + reconciliation logs.

Follow-ups for next sync
- Miguel to present canary results (router.fallback.rate) in next Tuesday sync.
- Rina to present auth rotation instrumentation and any compliance constraints.
- Evan to demo fast-reconcile PoC and dashboard tile.

Appendix (quick links)
- PLAT-4823: router judgment window canary
- AUTH-391: staggered rotation + grace accept
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane/pull/215 (Miguel proof-of-concept)
- Playbook draft: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PLAT/pages/Control+Plane+Fallback+Playbook

Notes-to-self: Keep this doc short — move full writeup into playbook page if canary shows improvement. If any oncall triggers the runbook, update the runbook with the concrete timestamps and diagnostic queries used.

End of recap.
